name: Built Robotics RPD 35
summary: A self-driving pile driver built on a Cat 335 excavator that carries up to 224 steel piles and drives them for solar trackers, paired with an RPS 25 robot that holds each pile in place.

germany.statusNote: Not offered in Germany: Built rents the piling system only as a robot-as-a-service with per-pile pricing and says it currently supports deployments in the United States and Australia only.

specs.label: Maximum payload
specs.conditions: sleds; Built's home page says 34,000 lb and its technology page 22,000 lb

specs.label: Pile lengths
specs.conditions: 2026 datasheet; the web page says 10–19 ft

specs.label: Maximum pile weight
specs.conditions: 2026 datasheet; the web page says 600 lb

specs.label: Pile cross sections
specs.conditions: 2026 datasheet; the web page says W6×7 to W8×28

specs.label: Companion robot RPS 25
specs.value: pile stabilizer on a Caterpillar 325 (65,000 lb, 8 psi); RTK GPS and LiDAR; pile twist and plumbness within ±1°; reveal window 0–10 ft
specs.conditions: accuracy is typical performance (1 standard deviation); web page gives a 0–8 ft reveal window

specs.label: Operating hours
specs.value: up to 24 hours a day in coordinated fleets

notes: Offered only as a service together with the RPS 25 stabilizer robot; every RPD 35 works with one RPS 25.
Needs a mini excavator with a pile attachment and a telehandler on site to load the pile baskets onto the sleds.
Payload is given only in pounds (40,000 lb on the sleds); the maker states no kg figures.
Works in mud (11 psi ground pressure, 1.6 ft ground clearance); the robot stops when its cameras detect a person nearby.

images.alt: Built Robotics RPD 35 pile driver with loaded pile sleds next to an RPS 25 stabilizer on a solar site at dusk

evidence.task: Announced as a fully autonomous solar pile driver; Built says a two-person crew can install over 300 piles per day
Drives steel piles for solar-panel foundations; nationwide deal for dozens of pile-driving robots
evidence.where: Blattner (Quanta Services), solar projects in the USA
evidence.note: Built was then deploying on its fourth project with Blattner; Blattner also plans to use the robots in Canada.

evidence.task: About 10 robots drive nearly 1,000 steel piles a day, more than half of the pile-driving scope, in the swampiest parts of a solar site
evidence.where: Solar project in northeastern Louisiana, USA, supplying Meta's Hyperion data center
evidence.note: Built is not a direct contractor for Meta.
